topicName: Query Optimizer Cost Model and Optimizer Hints
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"MySQL Query Optimizer Cost Model and Optimizer Hints"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The MySQL query optimizer is responsible for generating the most efficient execution plan for a given SQL statement. At the heart of this process is the cost model, which estimates the resource consumption of different execution strategies. Additionally, database administrators and developers can use optimizer hints to influence the optimizer when default choices are suboptimal."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the MySQL Cost Model"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The cost model assigns numerical cost values to various operations, such as reading rows from disk, evaluating expressions, and scanning index pages. These costs are categorized into I/O costs (disk reads) and CPU costs (processing rows). MySQL stores these configurable cost constants in the mysql.server_cost and mysql.engine_cost tables."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"mysql.server_cost: Contains general server-side costs like evaluating conditions and memory temporary table operations."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"mysql.engine_cost: Contains storage engine-specific costs, such as disk block reads and index evaluations, which can vary between InnoDB and MyISAM."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Inspecting and Modifying Cost Constants"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can inspect the current cost estimates by querying the mysql tables directly. If you want to adjust how the optimizer weighs certain operations globally or for specific sessions, you can update these values."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"SELECT cost_name, cost_value FROM mysql.server_cost;"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"To change the cost of memory-based temporary tables dynamically, use an UPDATE statement followed by a flush command to reload the optimizer cost model."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"UPDATE mysql.server_cost SET cost_value = 2.0 WHERE cost_name = 'row_evaluate_cost'; FLUSH OPTIMIZER_COSTS;"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Optimizer Hints"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"While the cost model works well for the vast majority of queries, complex schemas can sometimes lead to suboptimal execution plans. MySQL supports optimizer hints specified inside comments using the /*+ ... */ syntax. These hints instruct the optimizer to alter its behavior for a single statement."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Optimizer Hints"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"INDEX / NO_INDEX: Forces or prevents the optimizer from using specific indexes."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JOIN_ORDER / STRAIGHT_JOIN: Forces a specific order of table joins."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MRR: Controls Multi-Range Read optimization."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SET_VAR: Temporarily changes system variables for the duration of the query."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Practical Example Using Optimizer Hints"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a scenario where the optimizer incorrectly chooses a table scan over an index range scan. You can force the use of a specific index using the USE_INDEX hint as shown below."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"SELECT /*+ USE_INDEX(orders FOR SENDER, idx_customer_date) */ customer_id, order_date FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 105; "},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Another powerful hint is SET_VAR, which allows you to adjust session variables like sort_buffer_size inline without altering global performance configurations."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"SELECT /*+ SET_VAR(sort_buffer_size = 16M) */ * FROM large_table ORDER BY unindexed_column;"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering the MySQL cost model and leveraging optimizer hints gives database engineers fine-grained control over performance. Always rely on EXPLAIN statements to analyze the execution plan before and after applying cost model adjustments or query hints."}]
